name: Lithuania
summary_text: Lithuania is broadly workable, at the lower end, with one of Europe's most restrictive legal-gender-recognition situations. The Civil Code grants the right to medically change gender in principle, but there has been no legal framework regulating the procedure for 17 years — a deadlock the Constitutional Court refused to resolve in September 2025, perpetuating what an ECtHR body called a "distressing legal uncertainty." Socially, a conservative climate is well documented: an MP called LGBT people "degenerated" and "spreading diseases" (his immunity was revoked), "traditional family values" groups disrupt peaceful protests, the Seimas Ombudsperson found police failed to guarantee the LGBT community's right to assembly, and trans people report systemic workplace harassment — open ridicule, isolation, and psychological abuse. A "Protection of Minors" law limits dissemination of LGBT information (a 2024 Constitutional Court ruling weakened its same-sex-family provision). There is no criminalisation, and LT Pride 2024 drew 15,000.

sources.title: Constitutional Court Refuses to Address 18-Year Trans Rights Gap - LGL
sources.claim_summary: LGL (Lithuanian Gay League) news (Sept 2025): the Constitutional Court refused to address Lithuania's 18-year trans rights gap - a significant setback; the Civil Code grants unmarried adults the right to medically change gender but implementing legislation has never been adopted, leaving trans people in legal limbo.

sources.title: Could Courts Finally End 17 Years of Legal Limbo for Transgender Rights? - LGL
sources.claim_summary: LGL news (Aug 2025): could courts finally end 17 years of legal limbo for transgender rights? - the Ukmergė Chamber of the Vilnius Regional District Court suspended a civil case on amending civil-status gender documents and referred the question of the laws' compliance with the Constitution to the Constitutional Court.

sources.title: Lithuania’s top court declines to hear case on gender change in documents - LRT
sources.claim_summary: LRT (Sept 2025): Lithuania's Constitutional Court declined to examine a lower court's request to review the absence of legal provisions allowing trans people to change gender markers and personal identification codes in official documents.

sources.title: Mocked, isolated and ignored: Trans people in Lithuania detail workplace harassment - LRT
sources.claim_summary: LRT (May 2025): trans people in Lithuania detail workplace harassment - open ridicule, isolation and psychological abuse; systemic labour-market discrimination per experts.

sources.title: Seimas Ombudsperson: Lithuanian Police Failed to Guarantee LGBT Community’s Right to Peaceful Assembly - LGL
sources.claim_summary: LGL news (April 2024): the Seimas Ombudsperson found that police failed to guarantee the LGBT community's right to peaceful assembly - inadequate police response to hostile provocateurs at an LGL assembly; recommended measures to guarantee effective assembly rights.

Office of the Equal Opportunities Ombudsperson, 'The Situation of Transgender People in Lithuania - Summary of the National Review 2024': second national review (after 2019) covering public attitudes, the legal framework, document changes, healthcare barriers, labour-market discrimination, data protection and negative public attitudes; notes the lack of a legal framework and strategic approach.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025 (covering 2024) chapter on Lithuania: systemic lack of targeted LGBTI hate-crime victim support; LGBTI asylum seekers from Cameroon granted protection after a four-year wait, with dire camp conditions and a psychologist convicted of coercing asylum seekers into sexual acts; prosecution of former MP Gražulis for anti-LGBTI ridicule complicated by his MEP immunity.

sources.title: Lithuania: Parliament to consider five separate anti-gay and anti-trans bills | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Sept 2013): Lithuania's parliament to consider five anti-gay and anti-trans bills - a ban on gender reassignment ('gender is determined genetically from the very moment of conception'), a same-sex adoption ban, fines up to €1,800 for organisers of events 'denigrating constitutional moral values', and legalisation of anti-gay speech.

sources.title: Lithuania's parliament passes 'Section 28-style' law to ban homosexuality in schools | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (July 2009): Lithuania's parliament passed a 'Section 28-style' law banning information on homosexuality in schools and media accessible to minors ('Law on the Protection of Minors'), overriding President Adamkus's veto 87-6; Amnesty called it 'a huge step backwards'.
